To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the small kidney is the most important cause of renal artery stenosis in patients with renovascular disease; 2) the small kidney has the highest incidence of renal artery steno-occlusive lesions; 3) the small kidney, when associated with a stenosis of a renal artery, has a high incidence of contralateral renal artery stenoses, and 4) the small kidney should therefore be considered the most important lesion of renovascular hypertension.

in renovascular hypertension with a small kidney, percutaneous translumenal angioplasty of the stenosis of this kidney, if successful, results in cure of hypertension, and that nephrectomy of this kidney, even if the artery is occluded, results in improved blood pressure control.

in 57 patients treated with percutaneous translumenal arterioplasty and/or nephrectomy for renovascular hypertension associated one small kidney, 48 patients (84 per cent) were normotensive after a mean followup of 28 months.

the small kidney with poor renal perfusion is a major cause of renovascular hypertension.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the treatment of renovascular hypertension is a complex matter and that it is necessary to individualize treatment according to the patient's clinical and angiographic findings.
the treatment of renovascular hypertension associated to a small kidney is possible and effective if the patient is selected properly.
percutaneous transluminale arterioplasty is the treatment of choice in renovascular hypertension, and that it can be performed in most cases.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the small kidney can be a major contributor to hypertension.
percutaneous translumenal angioplasty (PCTA) should be the first-line treatment for renovascular hypertension (RVH).
patients with renovascular disease who have a small kidney and a high renin level should be treated with a combination of percutaneous translumenal revascularization and medical management.
